scenes.script_line: Now that you know what matters most, it's time for an honest look at the other side. Where is your life not working? In this step, you're identifying where your current experience isn't aligned with what truly matters to you. These might be areas that feel frustrating. Stuck. Inconsistent. Or not producing the results you know are possible.

shots.text: person sitting with a troubled, honest expression, looking at a workbook
close-up of a hand hovering over a page, hesitating
wide shot of a person sitting alone, surrounded by quiet

scenes.script_line: Notice the language here. We're not asking where you are failing. We're asking where your story isn't working for you. That's an important difference. The problem usually isn't you. It's the story you're running in that part of your life. How can you tell when a story isn't working? Look for repeating patterns. The same argument, again and again. The same ceiling you keep hitting at work. The same promise to yourself that never quite happens. When something keeps repeating, there is usually a story underneath it.

shots.text: two people talking quietly, one nodding in recognition
person staring at the same page of a notebook again, familiar frustration
close-up of a hand tapping a pen, repeating a thought

scenes.script_line: On page seven, you'll see a list of life areas. Career and business. Health. Money. Family. Relationships. Intimacy. Purpose. And a few more, including "something else." Read through them slowly, and notice your reaction to each one. The area that makes you pause, or wince a little, is often the one to work on. Here's the key instruction. Choose just one area. The one that feels most important, and that will create the greatest shift moving forward. It's tempting to fix everything at once. But this process goes deep, and depth needs focus. scenes.script_line: One more thing. Be careful not to pick the safest option. The area you'd rather avoid is often the one that holds the most energy for change. Once you've chosen, give your story a simple name. Sam chose career, and called it "the story that I'm not good enough to lead." Then write about why you selected this area. What's happening there? What is it costing you? How does it connect to what matters most from step one? Be honest, and be specific. Specific means real moments, not general feelings. scenes.script_line: And remember, naming what isn't working takes courage. It's the first real step toward changing it. Your facilitator will help you choose your area, and name the story you'll work on today.
